title: Serotonin syndrome (serotonin toxicity)
keyNumbers: Cyproheptadine: 12 mg initially, then 2 mg q2h while symptoms continue; maintenance 8 mg q6h (12–32 mg/24 h); oral only — crush via NG
Temperature >41 °C, rigidity, or hemodynamic instability → ICU
presentation: Onset usually within 24 h of a new serotonergic drug, dose increase, or interacting combination (e.g., linezolid, methylene blue, MAOIs, tramadol, fentanyl)
Neuromuscular: clonus (inducible, spontaneous, ocular), hyperreflexia, tremor — worse in legs; hypertonia in severe cases
Autonomic: hyperthermia, diaphoresis, tachycardia, mydriasis, diarrhea; agitation
definitions: Hunter criteria — serotonergic agent PLUS any of: spontaneous clonus; inducible clonus + agitation or diaphoresis; ocular clonus + agitation or diaphoresis; tremor + hyperreflexia; hypertonia + temperature >38 °C + ocular or inducible clonus (sens 84%, spec 97% vs toxicologist diagnosis)

immediateActions.action: Stop all serotonergic drugs; supportive care, IV fluids, continuous monitoring
Benzodiazepines; avoid physical restraints (isometric contraction worsens hyperthermia and lactic acidosis)
ICU: sedation, intubation, nondepolarizing paralysis; antipyretics don't work (heat is muscular); avoid succinylcholine

workup.test: Medication reconciliation incl. OTC/supplements and recent stops (fluoxetine washout is long)
BMP, CK, LFTs, coagulation, lactate, ABG
notes: Rhabdomyolysis, DIC, acidosis in severe cases

workup.test: Exclude mimics: infection (blood cultures; LP if indicated), NMS, anticholinergic toxicity, withdrawal, thyroid storm

treatment.doseText: Titrate to agitation and autonomic control
12 mg initially, then 2 mg q2h while symptoms continue; maintenance 8 mg q6h (12–32 mg/24 h); oral only — crush via NG
Not effective — hyperthermia is from muscle activity
Avoid — restraints worsen hyperthermia/acidosis; succinylcholine risks hyperkalemia with rhabdomyolysis

pitfalls: Clonus/hyperreflexia (worse in legs) points to serotonin syndrome; lead-pipe rigidity + bradyreflexia + slow onset points to NMS
Severe rigidity can mask clonus and hyperreflexia
Inpatient triggers: linezolid, methylene blue, fentanyl, tramadol, ondansetron/metoclopramide add-ons
Triptan + SSRI/SNRI rarely causes it: 0.6 definite cases/10,000 person-years (95% CI 0–1.5; 2.3 incl. possible cases) over 30,928 person-years of co-prescription; none life-threatening
escalateWhen: Temperature >41 °C, rigidity, or hemodynamic instability → ICU
sources: Boyer EW, Shannon M. The serotonin syndrome. N Engl J Med 2005;352(11):1112-1120. doi:10.1056/NEJMra041867
Dunkley EJC, et al. The Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria: simple and accurate diagnostic decision rules for serotonin toxicity. QJM 2003;96(9):635-642. doi:10.1093/qjmed/hcg109

Orlova Y, Rizzoli P, Loder E. Association of Coprescription of Triptan Antimigraine Drugs and Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor or Selective Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor Antidepressants With Serotonin Syndrome. JAMA Neurol 2018;75(5):566-572. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2017.5144
